patch.value: Domain-pack authoring kit: the reusable substrate for modeling a foreign domain — types, typed edges, invariants, projections, lifecycle — with a scaffold that proves it end to end

Two exemplars have proven the universal claim by construction: a minimal custom PM tool and a temporal digital-twin graph. Both were built by hand against SDK primitives, and neither left behind reusable substrate. The next author of a foreign domain repeats the same discovery work — which primitive models an entity, how to declare custom types and statuses, how to express an invariant that the engine will enforce rather than merely document, how to define a projection that stays bounded, how to attach domain lifecycle rules without forking the lifecycle engine. Package that path: a domain-pack shape with declared types, declared edge kinds and their semantics, declared invariants checked by validation, declared projections honoring the token budget, and declared lifecycle rules — plus a scaffold that generates a working pack and a conformance test that tells an author whether their pack is correct. The kit is also the honest test of the SDK boundary: every gap an author would hit is a missing SDK primitive, and finding those gaps is half the value of building it.

A domain pack declares custom types, custom edge kinds with their semantics, invariants, projections, and lifecycle rules through documented public SDK surface only, with no private core imports; Declared invariants are enforced by validation, so a pack can make an illegal state unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged; Declared projections honor the token budget and degrade deterministically, like core read surfaces; A scaffold generates a working pack, and a conformance test tells an author whether their pack is correct, with named failures rather than a generic error; Building the kit produces a filed item for every SDK gap encountered, linked to this item as discovered_from, and none are worked around privately; The kit is exercised by rebuilding at least one existing exemplar on top of it, proving it is sufficient rather than merely plausible
Modeling a foreign domain on pm is a declared pack, not a from-scratch integration project
The universal-platform milestone is unreachable while each domain is bespoke; a kit is what turns two proofs of concept into a repeatable capability
Formalizes the extension surface a domain author depends on, which raises the compatibility bar for that surface; gaps found while building it become SDK promotion work
A developer models a new domain in hours using declared substrate, and every gap they hit is a filed SDK primitive rather than a workaround
